articles.title: CM promises govt. support to India’s newest public health university coming up in Hyderabad
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy assured the Public Health Foundation of India (PHFI) of the State government’s full support for establishing its Institute of Public Health Sciences (IPHS) Deemed-to-be University in Hyderabad, setting June 2, 2028, as the deadline for completing the proposed campus and promising assistance with land, funds, permissions and other requirements.

Speaking at the foundation-laying ceremony and unveiling of the campus master plan on Saturday, Mr. Reddy said the government was committed to developing the institution into a world-class university that would contribute to public health education, research and healthcare in India and internationally.

He further added that the proposed university was not merely another educational institution but a project of global significance. Expressing confidence in its potential, he said he hoped that in the coming years, people would discuss the PHFI university alongside established institutions such as Harvard and Oxford.

The Chief Minister recalled how institutions such as the Indian School of Business (ISB) had contributed to Hyderabad’s emergence as an educational and knowledge hub. He said individuals who had established successful institutions had helped create a distinct identity for the city and that the PHFI university would add to this legacy.
PHFI Chairman Rajat Gupta said the university aspired to achieve excellence through world-class faculty, students, international collaborations and infrastructure.

PHFI IPHS Chancellor Dr. K. Srinath Reddy said PHFI aspired to become the world’s leading public health institution with the establishment of the university in Hyderabad. Dr. Reddy said the foundation’s work involved advancing multidisciplinary education and research through multi-sectoral implementation and multi-stakeholder engagement. The objective was to improve life expectancy, strengthen health systems, align policies across sectors with population health goals and encourage active community engagement.

Pro-Chancellor Sanjay Zodpey said the university was being conceived as a long-term institution that would serve generations of students, researchers, public health professionals and communities. He said the public health challenges of the 21st century required professionals with interdisciplinary perspectives, evidence-based knowledge and a commitment to equity and social impact.

Vice-Chancellor M. Vishnu Vardhana Rao outlined the university’s academic journey and expansion plans. The Indian Institute of Public Health Hyderabad was established in 2008 under the aegis of PHFI, with the objective of advancing public health through education, research and community engagement. The institution received recognition as a deemed-to-be university from the University Grants Commission in 2025, with Hyderabad as its main campus and Bengaluru as another campus, he said.

With the proposed campus and modern infrastructure, the institution plans to expand its academic offerings to at least six postgraduate programmes, two undergraduate programmes, PhD programmes and institute-level Master of Public Health programmes. It aims to build an academic community of approximately 2,500 students and research scholars over the next five years.

Dr. Rao said the university’s research priorities would include infectious diseases and pandemic preparedness, non-communicable diseases, maternal and child health, One Health, mental health and disability. Digital health, artificial intelligence and data science would serve as cross-cutting areas across its research activities, he added.

articles.title: BJP accuses Congress of double standard on women’s issues
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) on Saturday (November 14, 2026) accused the Congress of following a double standard on the issue of women’s dignity, safety and empowerment by publicly advocating women’s rights while “remaining silent” on accusations of misconduct against its own leaders.

At a press conference, BJP MP Bansuri Swaraj referred to Jharkhand Congress MLA Bhushan Bara, who has been accused of sexually assaulting a 14-year-old tribal girl; MP Bimol Akoijam, who faces allegations of sexual harassment in Jawaharlal Nehru University (JNU); and Uttarakhand party leader Harak Singh Rawat, who was earlier accused of raping a woman from Assam.
The woman, who claimed that she became pregnant after the alleged abuse, has now demanded a DNA test on her son. The three Congress leaders have denied the accusations.

Ms. Swaraj questioned the “silence” of senior Congress leaders, saying that under the leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi, the BJP government was empowering women to become self-reliant and nation-builders, while the Congress was limited to raising slogans.

She alleged that the Congress continued to “repeatedly insult women”. “Tomorrow also marks the birth anniversary of Bhagwan Birsa Munda ji and Janjatiya Gaurav Diwas. On such an occasion, it is deeply shameful that Jharkhand Congress MLA Bhushan Bara is facing serious allegations of sexually assaulting a 14-year-old tribal girl,” she said.

“It is surprising that the Congress, which raises hollow slogans such as ‘Smash the Patriarchy’, along with its Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi, Priyanka Gandhi, Sonia Gandhi and Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge, has once again chosen to maintain silence on this matter,” she alleged.

“All these cases are distinct from one another, whether it is the rape of a tribal girl, the appointment of Bimol Akoijam as co-chairman of manifesto committee, or the appointment of Harak Singh Rawat as chairman of the election management committee in Uttarakhand. However, one thing is common to all these cases: the conspicuous silence of the Congress party and Rahul Gandhi,” she said.

articles.title: Iron ore capacity under-utilisation in major-producing states prompt concerns as India sets 2047 target
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Budget & Banking
fullParagraphs: With India’s iron ore demand projected to rise to 772 million tonnes (MT) by 2047, miners in Odisha, the country’s largest iron ore reserve holder, are yet to utilise nearly 40% of their existing capacities, raising concerns over resource wastage and potential revenue losses.
The issue has come under judicial scrutiny, with both the Supreme Court earlier this month and the Odisha High Court in January flagging the underutilisation of mining capacities.

The Odisha High Court, while agreeing with petitioners who highlighted the sluggish operationalisation of mines despite environmental clearances, observed that the delay had resulted in an average annual revenue loss of ₹4,000 crore to the State.
However, industry sources, speaking on condition of anonymity, attributed the delays primarily to prolonged forest clearance procedures, which often exceed the stipulated 18-month timeframe.

Data cited by petitioner Citizens’ Action Forum (Bhubaneswar) show that of the 246 million tonnes per annum (MTPA) of mining capacity granted environmental clearance in FY25, only around 159 MTPA had been operationalised.

Separately, data published by mining consultancy BigMint in June 2026 show that Odisha produced 158 MT of iron ore in FY26 against an environmentally cleared capacity of 278 MTPA, indicating capacity utilisation of nearly 60%.
The underutilised capacity is particularly significant as it largely involves hematite, the highest-grade variety of iron ore.

The shortfall also raises questions over India’s continued dependence on imports. According to the Mines Ministry, the country imported 12.3 MT of iron ore in FY26, incurring an expenditure of ₹11,115 crore.

Odisha accounted for more than 50% of India’s domestic iron ore production during FY26. Chhattisgarh contributed around 17.1%, followed by Karnataka at 16.6%. Capacity utilisation in the two states – albeit with significantly lower volumes than Odisha – stood at 62% and 80%, respectively, according to calculations based on BigMint data.

In January, the Odisha High Court directed that mining rights be mandatorily transferred to state-owned National Mineral Development Corporation (NMDC) to ensure “optimum utilisation of the mines” and “eradicate any burden on the government exchequer”.

However, in its November 4 order, the Supreme Court concurred with the need for optimum utilisation of mineral resources but left the decision on transferring mining rights to the State government’s discretion, rather than making it mandatory.

articles.title: India's exports up 29.9% in October; trade deficit narrows to $20.09 billion
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Budget & Banking
fullParagraphs: India’s merchandise exports rose to an all-time high of $49.5 billion in October 2026, bringing down the country’s overall trade deficit, official data released on Friday showed.
While a large part of this growth was due to petroleum products, Commerce Secretary Rajesh Agrawal said diversification of exports to various locations helped improve the numbers.
India’s total exports, including goods and services, stood at $89.99 billion in October 2026, up nearly 30% from last October.
The overall trade deficit shrank from $25.1 billion last October to $20.1 billion year-on-year.

“In the month of October, the exports of merchandise exports have registered a new peak of $49.47 billion,” Mr. Agrawal said at a press briefing. “This is the highest-ever monthly merchandise export value, along with the highest monthly growth of 45.03% in the last five years.”
Merchandise imports rose to a record high of $89.35 billion in October 2026, up 16.5% YoY. Total imports stood at $110.1 billion, a 16.6% increase.

According to trade experts, goods exports growing faster than merchandise imports shows that while the rise in global prices contributed to the increase in the value of India’s exports, there was also an increase in the underlying export volumes.

“The particularly encouraging part of this growth is that this is not in any particular sector, this is not in any particular geography, it is broad-based across countries and regions,” Mr. Agrawal added. “43 of our 50 top export destinations posted positive growth in October 2026 as compared to 2025.”
The data show that India’s exports to 12 out of its top 20 export destinations grew by double digits or more.
Mr. Agrawal pointed out that India’s exports to its free trade agreement (FTA) partners had grown strongly.
One of the key areas of diversification has been the African continent, with exports to that region growing 44% in April-September 2026 to $31.4 billion.
Notably, India’s trade with West Asia is recovering as countries find alternate routes and ports other than those along the constrained Strait of Hormuz.

fullParagraphs: What Disneyland is to children today, Lavi Fair in Rampur Bushahr, in Himachal Pradesh’s Shimla district, was to my family in the 1980s. I recall wandering through the fair as an eight-year-old, watching an old man smoking a chillum beside heaps of black sheep fleece and stacks of white woollen pattus (traditional garments of Kinnaur and Kullu women).

Mother and her friends carefully chose shawls for their daughters’ and future daughters-in-law’s trousseaux. Years later, I received a beautiful black sheep wool and pashmina shawl for my wedding. Wool finds pride of place at the fair. The name Lavi is linked to “Loe”, a sheet of woollen cloth and the practice of shearing sheep.

articles.title: How did a tax proposal lead the Dutch government to the verge of collapse? | Explained
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Budget & Banking
fullParagraphs: Story so far: The Dutch government came close to a collapse this week over its Tax Plan for 2027 as members of the three-party ruling coalition disagreed over an amendment to the plan. Though the plan was passed in the lowest-possible majority in the House of Representatives on Thursday (November 12, 2026) night and the government subsequently defeated a no-confidence motion, the developments have brought a rift in the coalition out in the open and threaten the future of the government led by Rob Jetten just nine-months into its 4-year term.

The Netherlands currently has a minority government by a coalition of three parties holding 66 seats in the 150-member Tweede Kamer, the lower house. The centrist D66 led by Prime Minister Jetten, the youngest premier in the country’s history, is the single largest party with 26 seats and is joined by centre-right parties People’s Party for Freedom and Democracy (VVD) and Christian Democratic Appeal (CDA), with 22 and 18 seats respectively. The government came to power in February, 117 days after a snap election in October last year necessitated by the collapse of Dick Schoof’s right-wing government as far-right leader of Freedom Party Geert Wilders withdrew his support. The months following the election that failed to produce a clear winner saw parties across political spectrum and ideologies negotiate to form a government to no effect, paving the way for the centrist parties to make do with a minority administration.

articles.title: India needs to create high-quality jobs, increase productivity growth: IMF
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Budget & Banking
fullParagraphs: India would need higher productivity growth, stronger private investment and faster creation of high-quality jobs to achieve the medium-term potential growth of 6.8%, the International Monetary Fund (IMF) said on Thursday (November 12, 2026).
In its October World Economic Outlook, the IMF had upgraded India’s medium-term potential growth to 6.8% from its earlier estimate of 6.5%.

The upgrade took into account a few factors, including favourable demographics, a large and growing domestic economy or domestic market for goods, and continued momentum on structural reforms, Julie Kozack, Communications Director, IMF, told reporters in Washington.

“But in general, like in many countries, we are encouraging India to take continuing reforms, particularly to focus on how productivity growth can be increased,” she said in response to a question from PTI .
The IMF official said that to further the medium-term potential, India would need higher productivity growth, stronger private investment, and faster creation of high-quality jobs.
Ms. Kozack said these issues will come up during the Article 4 consultations with India.
Last month, the IMF raised India’s growth forecast for fiscal year 2027 and fiscal year 2028 to 7%, from the 6.4% and 6.7% projections respectively made in July.
“India does remain a key growth engine for the world. The economy has strong fundamentals and has shown considerable resilience,” Ms. Kozack said.

articles.title: Amidst Indus water tensions, Pakistan to send vocal critic to SCO Civilisational Dialogue; first Ministerial visit in three years
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Foreign Visits & UN/G20/BRICS
fullParagraphs: The first Pakistani Minister to visit India in more than three years, Musadik Masood Malik, has been a vocal critic of New Delhi’s decision to place the Indus Waters Treaty “in abeyance” following the April 2025 Pahalgam terrorist attack.

Dr. Malik is Pakistan’s Federal Minister for Climate Change and Environmental Coordination and will represent his country at the Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO) Civilisational Dialogue to be held here from November 20 to 22, Islamabad announced on Saturday.
The last Pakistani Minister to visit India was Bilawal Bhutto who had visited Goa in May 2023 for the SCO Foreign Ministers meeting.

JUST IN | Pakistan has nominated Federal Minister for Climate Change and Environmental Coordination, Dr. Musadik Masood Malik, to represent the country at the SCO Civilisational Dialogue, scheduled to be held in New Delhi from November 20 to November 22. - @suhasinih reports 📸 Special Arrangement

The Hindu had reported on October 28 that the Indian government had invited Pakistan’s Minister for National Heritage and Culture Aurungzeb Khan Khichi to attend the SCO Civilisational Dialogue event, the first such Ministerial-level invitation since 2023. However, the Pakistani government has nominated a different representative.

“The Government of Pakistan remains committed to promoting dialogue among civilisations and fostering people to people contacts within the SCO framework in a spirit of mutual respect,” the Pakistan government said in a statement on Saturday.

India and Pakistan engaged in military hostilities after the terror attack in Pahalgam, following which India placed the 1960 Indus Waters Treaty (IWT) “in abeyance”. Mr. Malik, a technocrat turned Minister, said in a press conference in June this year that Pakistan would “cut off those hands” that are attempting to control the Indus waters.

Asserting its claim on the Indus, Pakistan has been highlighting the Indus Valley civilisation of Mohenjodaro and Harappa and other ancient sites in the country in recent months. On World Heritage Day on April 18, Pakistan Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif had referred to the Indus Valley civilisation in his remarks, saying, “Pakistan’s cultural heritage is enriched with a multifaceted civilisation. Our homeland carries the legacy of some of the world’s oldest civilisations, reflecting a vibrant tapestry of human creativity and diversity.”

On Friday (November 13, 2026), Union Culture Minister Gajendra Singh Shekhawat said India and Pakistan have a shared “civilisational and cultural” past, adding that New Delhi hopes that Pakistan will attend the upcoming SCO Civilisational Dialogue. China, Kazakhstan, Iran, Tajikistan, and Uzbekistan are among the countries that have already confirmed their participation.

“I believe that Pakistan’s civilisational and cultural progress is no different from ours,” Mr. Shekhawat said, in response to a question about the invitation, given the tensions with Pakistan. “They [Pakistan] separated from us less than 100 years ago, but prior to that, we [India and Pakistan] have evolved together. So we should not have any differences over these issues,” he added.

Mr. Shekhawat said that the purpose of the SCO Civilisational Dialogue, first proposed by Prime Minister Narendra Modi, was to see how the SCO could “go a step beyond geopolitical, strategic and bilateral relations and strengthen our cultural ties so that in the future we can have better relations and communications between the people of our countries.”

Soon after Mr. Shekhawat’s comments, however, the Ministry of External Affairs said that India would follow “national policy” regarding Pakistan in view of the Pahalgam terror attacks, indicating that it may not grant Punjab Chief Minister Bhagwant Singh Mann clearance to attend an international Punjabi cultural conference in Lahore at the end of the month.

articles.title: Rubio acknowledges ’people are struggling’ economically in speech after GOP midterm wipeout
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Foreign Visits & UN/G20/BRICS
fullParagraphs: Secretary of State Marco Rubio gave a sweeping speech to fellow conservatives on Friday evening (November 13, 2026), acknowledging that Americans are struggling in the current economy, while also railing against what he called the “weaponisation” of international law to constrain the U.S. from acting in its own interests.
His comments to the conservative Federalist Society touched on a core issue of the midterm elections — economic pain — that U.S. voters cited in delivering massive losses to Rubio's Republican Party.

“I think we have to recognise that people are struggling. There’s no doubt about it,” he said. “The health of our economy has nothing to do with the stock market. The health of their economy is whether they have enough money to be able to afford the things they need.”

President Donald Trump often points to the stock market as evidence that the economy is doing well. But voters, angry over higher costs, gave Democrats control of Congress after blaming Trump for his tariffs, his war in Iran and his unfulfilled campaign promise two years ago to bring down prices.

Mr. Rubio's remarks had the overtones of campaign speech, though the former Florida senator has consistently refused to discuss whether he would seek the presidency in 2028 in a race that could pit him against Vice President J.D. Vance. Mr. Rubio gave another wide-ranging speech last month in Greece that focused on Western values and also appeared to reflect his political aspirations beyond being America’s top diplomat.
ALSO WATCH U.S. midterm elections: What India is watching after Trump’s setback | Worldview

Mr. Rubio on Friday (November 13, 2026) defended the Iran war, arguing that it was necessary to stop the threat of the Islamic Republic obtaining a nuclear weapon. But he acknowledged that the unpopular conflict has driven up gasoline prices for Americans and other connected costs.

“It’s not easy to address these things because it’s not popular to address them," Mr. Rubio said. “It’s difficult. And oftentimes it inflicts, you know, pain, economic pain and otherwise. So we recognise that.”

He also pointed to the need for American leaders to continue a tradition of ensuring the next generation is better off than those before them. Economic prosperity is “not self-perpetuating,” he said, but an enormous undertaking that requires years and decades and is not accomplished “election cycle to election cycle."

“That’s the challenge before us now, because I do think there’s a legitimate fear that we will be the first generation to leave the next worse off, and that can’t happen. That’s un-American,” he said.

Mr. Rubio also hit back hard at critics of Trump administration's policies, such as deadly strikes on alleged drug-smuggling boats in Latin America, the January capture of then-Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro and strict immigration policies.
He accused other countries and international organisations of trying to stymie the U.S. from acting in its own best interests by accusing the Trump administration of violations of international law.

articles.title: Trump tells advisers he may hold off on Iran attacks barring new provocations, sources say
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Foreign Visits & UN/G20/BRICS
fullParagraphs: U.S. President Donald Trump has told senior advisers in recent ​days that he may hold off on attacking Iran if the U.S. faces no new provocations from Tehran or the Iran-backed Houthis in Yemen, according to three people familiar ‌with the matter.

Mr. Trump has alternated between threats of escalating the war with new strikes and winding down hostilities, ​and current and former officials say he does not appear to have made up his mind about how to resolve the ⁠unpopular conflict, which he launched in February with Israel.

But in meetings with his national security advisers and after a series of intelligence briefings, Mr. Trump said he was considering holding off on strikes, said the people, who, like others interviewed for this story, spoke on condition of anonymity.
He has also indicated sympathy for allies in the region ‌who have asked him not to return to a full-fledged war.

"I could end it immediately, but at the request of the nations that I am looking to protect, we are doing it a little bit longer way, a bit more civilly," Mr. Trump ‌told sports broadcaster Stephen A. Smith on Thursday.

The war has hiked global fuel prices and proven unpopular with U.S. voters, who handed control ‌of ⁠Congress to the Democrats in last week's midterm elections. In a Reuters /Ipsos poll taken shortly before the November 3 elections, 55% ⁠of Americans said the war was not worth the cost, and Vice-President J.D. Vance cited it as the reason Mr. Trump's Republicans lost Congress.
Mr. Trump's private comments build on public remarks playin down the likelihood of major warfare resuming.

"As Commander-in-Chief, President Trump is the architect and sole decision-maker who holds all the cards and will always ensure that America’s interests are ​protected," a White House official said in a statement. "The United States ‌is in a very strong position with control of the Strait of Hormuz and the Iranian economy collapsing. Only President Trump knows what he will do, and when."
The CIA and Office of the Director of National Intelligence did not respond to requests for comment.

In phone calls over the past two weeks, Mr. Trump asked for opinions from Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman and Turkish President ‌Tayyip Erdogan, who both urged him not to resume attacks on Iran, according to a senior U.S. official and another person familiar ​with the matter. They said Mr. Trump made no commitment either way.

Mr. Trump told Mr. bin Salman on October 31 that he was planning to attack after the elections, but the crown prince pleaded for him to hold off, arguing that economic sanctions ⁠against Iran were working, according to two more people familiar with the discussion.
Saudi Arabia's Foreign Ministry did not respond to a request for comment.

articles.title: India supports UNGA resolution on permanent sovereignty of Palestinian people
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Foreign Visits & UN/G20/BRICS
fullParagraphs: India has voted in favour of a UN General Assembly draft resolution that reaffirms the inalienable rights of the Palestinian people and the population of the occupied Syrian Golan over their natural resources and demands that Israel cease the exploitation and damage of these resources.

The 193-Member UN General Assembly voted overwhelmingly on Wednesday (November 11, 2026) in favour of the resolution ‘Permanent sovereignty of the Palestinian people in the Occupied Palestinian Territory, including East Jerusalem, and of the Arab population in the occupied Syrian Golan over their natural resources’ proposed by Uruguay.
India voted in favour of the resolution along with 150 other UN Member States, while Israel and the U.S. were among the seven nations that voted against the draft, which got 11 abstentions.
The resolution reaffirmed the inalienable rights of the Palestinian people and of the population of the occupied Syrian Golan over their natural resources, including land, water and energy resources.

It demanded that Israel “cease the exploitation, damage, cause of loss or depletion and endangerment of the natural resources in the Occupied Palestinian Territory, including East Jerusalem, and in the occupied Syrian Golan .

It stressed that the wall and settlements being constructed by Israel in the Occupied Palestinian Territory, including in and around East Jerusalem, are contrary to international law and seriously deprive the Palestinian people of their natural resources.
It also called for full compliance with the legal obligations affirmed in the July 2004 advisory opinion of the International Court of Justice and relevant UN resolutions.

The resolution called upon Israel to comply strictly with its obligations under international law, including international humanitarian law, and immediately and completely cease all policies and measures aimed at altering the character and status of the Occupied Palestinian Territory, including East Jerusalem.

It further called upon Israel to halt all actions, including those perpetrated by Israeli settlers, that harm the environment, including the dumping of waste materials in the Occupied Palestinian Territory, including East Jerusalem, and the occupied Syrian Golan.

It also called upon Israel to cease its destruction of vital infrastructure, including water pipelines, sewage networks and electricity networks, and to cease its demolition and confiscation of Palestinian homes and civilian infrastructure, agricultural lands and water wells.
It also stressed the urgent need to advance reconstruction and development projects in this regard, including in the Gaza Strip, and called for support for the necessary efforts in this regard.

articles.title: Quad Summit likely to be held in Manila on November 17, sources say
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Foreign Visits & UN/G20/BRICS
fullParagraphs: Prime Minister Narendra Modi will meet U.S. President Donald Trump, Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi and Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese at the first Quad Summit since 2024 this week in Manila, on the sidelines of ASEAN summits, sources in New Delhi confirmed to The Hindu . The meeting is expected to take place on November 17 evening, the sources said, adding that it would probably take place after Mr. Trump lands in Manila.

While the confirmation of the Quad Summit in Manila is significant for the Indo-Pacific grouping, and plans to chart out their next course, much of the attention will be taken by Mr. Trump’s pronouncements at his next stop in Shenzhen, China, where he will hold the first-ever three-way summit with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin on November 19, to discuss global issues including nuclear arms control.

In Washington, U.S. officials briefing media on Mr. Trump’s travels also confirmed that the US President will travel to Manila and, among other meetings, will take part in a “multilateral meeting” with Quad country leaders, news agency Reuters reported.

The agency quoted an official briefing by unnamed officials who said that supply chains for critical minerals and securing commercial shipping lanes for energy supplies would be a key part of the agenda. “The issue of attacks on commercial ships is very likely to ​be taken up,” the unnamed official quoted by Reuters said. The safety of ships and seafarers has been a particularly important issue for India, as at least 30 Indian seafarers aboard ships in the Hormuz Strait, the Sea of Oman, and the Black Sea have been killed in attacks during the conflicts in Iran and Ukraine, respectively. Earlier, reports had indicated that a Quad Business Forum mechanism would also be announced during the Summit.

The Manila meeting will be the first Quad Summit to be held in a non-Quad country and indicates the challenges that India has faced as the Chair of the Summit of the four-country grouping that revived its cooperation in the Indo-Pacific in 2017, upgrading it during the COVID-19 pandemic in 2021 to leader-level meetings. Since then, the government has been unable to host the Quad Summit in India even once, mainly due to the U.S. President’s unavailability. New Delhi is unwilling to hand over the Chairship of the summit without hosting it here either, which may yet happen in Delhi next year, the sources told The Hindu .

Officials didn’t clarify on who will be the official host of the meeting in Manila, which has been discussed for weeks, including during U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio’s visits to India this year in May and October. The US midterm election results, in which the ruling Republican Party lost its majorities in the U.S. Congress, had delayed the confirmation of Mr. Trump’s travels to the Philippines for the East Asia Summit and to China for the Asia Pacific Economic Cooperation Summit.

On Friday (November 13, 2026), when asked at a briefing, government spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal told journalists only that the MEA would “keep [them] updated with developments in Manila pertaining to the Quad”. On Saturday (November 14, 2026) evening, officials who confirmed the Summit would take place late on Tuesday evening (November 17, 2026) said they were still awaiting a formal intimation of the timing.

articles.title: Myanmar airstrike on displaced persons camp kills 12, say witnesses
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Foreign Visits & UN/G20/BRICS
fullParagraphs: A Myanmar military airstrike on a camp housing people displaced by the civil war killed 12 people in the westernmost state of Rakhine, witnesses and a rescue worker said on Saturday (November 14, 2026).

Chit Su Wai, a 27-year-old shopkeeper, sobbed as she described how her daughter, aunt and mother were killed on Friday evening (November 13, 2026) in Byar La IDP camp in Ponnagyun township, northeast of state capital Sittwe.

"All I saw was their bodies scattered in pain. I could not find words to describe it. And we were lost with crying," she said. "It has broken our family. There were no others except my family. We did not hear the sound of the fighter jet — it just came and dropped the bombs."
Myanmar army seizes key resistance headquarters and 10 bases held by opposition, state media says

Myanmar has been consumed by civil war since the military staged a coup five years ago, provoking armed resistance from democracy activists and ethnic minority factions that have long held sway in the nation's fringes.

The western coastal state of Rakhine is among the regions worst hit by the war. Controlled almost entirely by the ethnic minority Arakan Army (AA), it has been blockaded by the military and pummelled with regular airstrikes. It was not possible to contact the Myanmar military for comment on the latest attack.

Chit Su Wai said 12 people died in Friday's attack, a toll confirmed by Khine Hein Htet, chairman of the Phyusin Yin Khwin Foundation, a rescue and emergency service. Khine Hein Htet said a five-year-old was among the dead, while 18 were also injured in the camp, where many residents had been living for four years.

"They believed the camp was safe, and they sheltered there together. When we arrived at the scene, most of the victims had died in one place," the 24-year-old said. He said it was not a combat area, adding: "We never thought this camp would be targeted."

The village was a mess of collapsed bamboo houses on Saturday, the wreckage of an upturned vehicle mixed among the debris of household goods and clothes. Locals had already removed the bodies, wrapping them in yellow and red plastic and burying them in makeshift graves.

Aung Kyaw Min, a 45-year-old tuktuk driver, described how he rushed to the village where his brother and sister lived after hearing of the attack. "My sister's body was already headless while my brother was lying dead," he said, crying.

The next day, he discovered his mother had also been killed, while other relatives, including a 10-year-old, were missing. His sister was a seamstress who took care of their mother. His brother was a tuktuk driver like him.

"Now all of them — my sister, brother, including my mother — were all killed. My niece and nephews are still missing, I don't know where to find them," he said. The ACLED monitor estimates that more than 1,00,000 people have been killed in Myanmar on all sides since the civil war began.

articles.title: Anthropic’s valuation can’t secure its moat
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Updates, Tech & Climate Reports
fullParagraphs: Artificial intelligence (AI) company Anthropic, best known as the maker of the Claude AI model, is preparing to go public at a valuation of $1.4 trillion, which could make the IPO one of the largest in history. However, this particular refrain has of late seemed more ominous than cause for optimism, and the Anthropic IPO could be no exception.

The company has said it will offer 825 million shares at $70-78 apiece, to raise up to $64.4 billion. The valuation includes shares to be issued through employee options and other arrangements, and its market capitalisation based on outstanding shares is likely to be near $1 trillion. (It was valued at $965 billion in a private funding round in May.)

Anthropic’s financial prospects depend on continuing to spend extraordinary sums of money. Its amended prospectus filed with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission on November 10 revealed roughly $900 billion in spending commitments, almost entirely for computing infrastructure, until 2045. Of this, the company expects to incur half by 2030 and $70.7 billion in the twelve months from September 30.
The filing also mentions another $150-175 billion in potential payments under arrangements sans fixed dollar commitments.
These figures clarify a colossal exposure to future demand that neither Anthropic nor other Big AI companies have thus far been able to guarantee.

And while Anthropic’s revenue has also been growing, from $2.5 billion in the first three quarters of 2025 to $33.2 billion in the corresponding slice of 2026, the proposed fully diluted valuation exceeds annualised sales 17-fold.

The current business model is, largely, to charge customers according to how many tokens they use to run their tasks on its AI models. From January to September 2026, this revenue constituted 79% of the total revenue, giving Anthropic a reason to encourage users to maximise token use, irrespective of changes in the value of the output generated — a tendency famously called tokenmaxxing. But three factors complicate this picture. First, Anthropic has said AI models released within the last six months accounted for more than 80% of its third quarter revenue, which means its engineers need to keep building progressively more capable models. Second, it has not established that it will be able to sustain its profitability after honouring its infrastructure commitments.
The third factor is the most important, however: neither Anthropic nor its competitors, including OpenAI, currently has a lasting competitive advantage, a.k.a. a moat.

In fact, the difficulties of securing a moat are better illustrated by OpenAI CEO Sam Altman’s position of late, in favour of new regulatory and compliance demands. These demands could impose costs that larger AI companies will bear more easily than smaller ones.

Legitimate reasons to regulate AI include security failures and the risks posed by autonomous systems but governments should endeavour overtly to prevent such regulatory capture given the perverse incentives facing AI companies.

Overall, neither Anthropic nor its competitors have presented evidence of a sturdy moat. Instead, thanks to capable open-source development, models are becoming cheaper and competitors are catching up, and efficiency gains threaten the pricing power on which their valuations depend.

articles.title: CM promises govt. support to India’s newest public health university coming up in Hyderabad
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Updates, Tech & Climate Reports
fullParagraphs: Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy assured the Public Health Foundation of India (PHFI) of the State government’s full support for establishing its Institute of Public Health Sciences (IPHS) Deemed-to-be University in Hyderabad, setting June 2, 2028, as the deadline for completing the proposed campus and promising assistance with land, funds, permissions and other requirements.

Speaking at the foundation-laying ceremony and unveiling of the campus master plan on Saturday, Mr. Reddy said the government was committed to developing the institution into a world-class university that would contribute to public health education, research and healthcare in India and internationally.

He further added that the proposed university was not merely another educational institution but a project of global significance. Expressing confidence in its potential, he said he hoped that in the coming years, people would discuss the PHFI university alongside established institutions such as Harvard and Oxford.

The Chief Minister recalled how institutions such as the Indian School of Business (ISB) had contributed to Hyderabad’s emergence as an educational and knowledge hub. He said individuals who had established successful institutions had helped create a distinct identity for the city and that the PHFI university would add to this legacy.
PHFI Chairman Rajat Gupta said the university aspired to achieve excellence through world-class faculty, students, international collaborations and infrastructure.

PHFI IPHS Chancellor Dr. K. Srinath Reddy said PHFI aspired to become the world’s leading public health institution with the establishment of the university in Hyderabad. Dr. Reddy said the foundation’s work involved advancing multidisciplinary education and research through multi-sectoral implementation and multi-stakeholder engagement. The objective was to improve life expectancy, strengthen health systems, align policies across sectors with population health goals and encourage active community engagement.

Pro-Chancellor Sanjay Zodpey said the university was being conceived as a long-term institution that would serve generations of students, researchers, public health professionals and communities. He said the public health challenges of the 21st century required professionals with interdisciplinary perspectives, evidence-based knowledge and a commitment to equity and social impact.

Vice-Chancellor M. Vishnu Vardhana Rao outlined the university’s academic journey and expansion plans. The Indian Institute of Public Health Hyderabad was established in 2008 under the aegis of PHFI, with the objective of advancing public health through education, research and community engagement. The institution received recognition as a deemed-to-be university from the University Grants Commission in 2025, with Hyderabad as its main campus and Bengaluru as another campus, he said.

With the proposed campus and modern infrastructure, the institution plans to expand its academic offerings to at least six postgraduate programmes, two undergraduate programmes, PhD programmes and institute-level Master of Public Health programmes. It aims to build an academic community of approximately 2,500 students and research scholars over the next five years.

Dr. Rao said the university’s research priorities would include infectious diseases and pandemic preparedness, non-communicable diseases, maternal and child health, One Health, mental health and disability. Digital health, artificial intelligence and data science would serve as cross-cutting areas across its research activities, he added.

articles.title: Air pollution does not recognise State boundaries, coordinated action required: Union Minister
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Updates, Tech & Climate Reports
fullParagraphs: Saying that air pollution does not recognise State boundaries, Union Minister for Environment, Forest and Climate Change Bhupender Yadav on Saturday (November 14, 2026) emphasised the need for the coordinated implementation of pollution control measures across the National Capital Region (NCR), with real-time monitoring through Integrated Command and Control Centres (ICCCs) and direct accountability of field officers for violations.

At a review meeting held to assess measures undertaken by Delhi, Haryana, Uttar Pradesh, and Rajasthan to mitigate air pollution in Delhi-NCR, he directed all agencies to move beyond planning and ensure rigorous, time-bound, and coordinated enforcement on the ground.

The Minister directed State governments to nominate secretary-level officials for seven cities in Haryana, four cities in U.P., and four cities in Rajasthan to make them responsible for the implementation of pollution control measures through field visits and report to Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM) on a weekly basis.

The Minister directed all concerned States to install Automatic Number-plate Recognition (ANPR) cameras at fuel stations, integrated with VAHAN and Pollution Under Control Certificate (PUCC) databases, for intensified action against old and polluting vehicles, failing which CAQM would initiate criminal prosecution against delinquent Transport Department officials after November 30.

The Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB) was directed to immediately seal the identified 191 non-conforming polluting industries, which had not even placed orders for the installation of air pollution control devices (APCDs) despite repeated directions.

Calling for strict implementation of the Graded Response Action Plan (GRAP), Mr. Yadav called on NCR States to adopt Delhi’s hotspot-focused winter action plan, covering traffic management, work-from-home measures, construction restrictions and the prevention of open burning. Noting that only 3,221 km of the targeted 5,480 km of roads had been redeveloped, he directed road-owning agencies to prioritise pothole repairs, damaged footpaths, central verges, and end-to-end paving as per the CAQM framework, along with AI-based videographic surveys.

For traffic decongestion, the Union Minister directed immediate action at the 233 identified congestion points across NCR, and fresh assessments by the respective States. The Municipal Corporation of Delhi was asked to complete the installation of multi-lane free flow systems at 154 Delhi border entry points by December 31.

Mr. Yadav said that real-time inputs from sensors, cameras, and satellites must be used alongside physical inspections to identify violations and ensure swift enforcement. “Coordinated efforts, field-level accountability, and visible action on the ground are essential to effectively address the challenge of air pollution in Delhi-NCR,” he said.

articles.title: Age of AI: behind Tarluvada’s blue wall in Visakhapatnam
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Updates, Tech & Climate Reports
fullParagraphs: The muddy, unpaved road into Tarluvada runs along a wall of tall blue corrugated iron sheets. Once, it was just farms and forests. What is being built behind the wall is hidden from view. Just beyond, on the hill locals call Chukka Konda, a broad swathe of the slope has been stripped back to red earth and cut into terraces, stark against the green around it.

Last year, when government officials came to the small village in Anandapuram mandal on the outskirts of Visakhapatnam in Andhra Pradesh, they had made big promises: plentiful jobs and opportunities once Google, the American tech corporation, built its hyperscale 1 GW AI data centre there. Today, the village is uneasy. Many farmers refuse to talk. Leaders of Left parties say they are not allowed to meet the locals to understand their problems, and those who speak to them are being targeted and harassed by the police.

articles.title: ‘Abki baar, AQI 400-paar’: Congress takes a swipe at Modi over Delhi pollution
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Updates, Tech & Climate Reports
fullParagraphs: The Congress on Saturday (November 14, 2026) took a swipe at Prime Minister Narendra Modi over his 2024 Lok Sabha election slogan, “Abki baar, 400-paar”, saying it had come true in the national capital, with Delhi’s air quality index (AQI) crossing the 400-mark.
In a post in Hindi on X, Congress general secretary Jairam Ramesh said, “Abki baar, AQI 400-paar. The ‘pravachanmantri’s’ (preaching minister) slogan is coming true when it comes to AQI!”

Referring to reports of worsening air quality in Delhi, Mr. Ramesh said the city had become the most polluted in the world, with toxic air making breathing difficult. Children and the elderly were bearing the brunt of the pollution, while the number of patients in hospitals was rising, he said.
“Slogans were tossed into the air; now the air itself has turned to poison,” he said.
Mr. Modi had used the “Abki baar, 400-paar” slogan during the 2024 Lok Sabha election campaign, seeking a mandate of more than 400 seats for the National Democratic Alliance.

Several air quality monitoring stations in Delhi have recorded AQI levels in the ‘severe’ category (400-500) over the past few days. The city’s average AQI had also crossed the 400-mark on Friday (November 13, 2026).

articles.title: Critical ban: On recycling of lithium-ion batteries
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: On November 10, the Directorate General of Foreign Trade banned the export of lithium-ion battery black mass by moving it from the “free” to the “prohibited” list of exports. Black mass is an intermediate product when spent batteries and factory scrap are shredded. It contains valuable lithium, nickel, cobalt, manganese and graphite. The Commerce Ministry says the ban will ensure feedstock for domestic refiners, lift their capacity utilisation and draw investment. While the recycling of lead-acid batteries end-to-end is an established ecosystem and formalised, too, lithium-ion battery recycling is an emerging segment with only a few dozen licensed operators but has much potential given the scale of use of such batteries in EVs. While the ban will redirect supply, it will not automatically create a market and ecosystem. Just banning export without creating an entire ecosystem will only lead to dumping of lithium-ion batteries into landfills if the blackmass has no market. Blackmass production is a largely mechanical process but further downstream processing is more specialised chemical processing requiring larger investment and further policy support. If downstream units are online, their output can directly feed into indigenous lithium-ion battery manufacture.

India depends heavily on imports for critical minerals such as those used in battery inputs. Beyond working on supply aspects, the government must address the price gap to create a robust recycling market. Under the Battery Waste Management Rules, 2022, producers buy extended producer responsibility (EPR) certificates from recyclers but these are undervalued. Cheap certificates reward recycling on paper over investment in high-yield plants. A floor price that covers the full cost of recovery, with digital tracking, would fix that. Rare earths show how recycling remains a missed opportunity for India because of policy gaps. A smartphone can be up to 1% neodymium-iron-boron magnet by weight. That puts its rare earth content at about 3,000 parts per million, comparable to India’s monazite beach sands. Extracting it takes less energy than mining. A magnet separated from the phone is about 30% rare earth. Magnets make up as much as 3% of a hard drive, but are usable only if they are removed before the drive is shredded for data destruction. Yet the e-waste rules do not require rare earth separation. Rare earths need a separate EPR category, too. Payment by weight cannot be applied for rare earth minerals.

articles.title: In a dilemma: On Sheikh Hasina and India-Bangladesh ties
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: Bangladesh’s former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina now in exile in India, has set off speculation about her imminent return to Dhaka by submitting an application for a new Bangladeshi passport and national identity card this week. The application, made through the Bangladesh High Commission in Delhi, was dismissed by Prime Minister Tarique Rahman’s Foreign Affairs Adviser Humayun Kabir, who said that the government in Dhaka would not grant a passport to a “terrorist”, and would seek her return via the extradition agreement as a “prisoner transfer process” with India. Ms. Hasina has already announced that she plans to return to Bangladesh in December this year, as she did after her previous stay in India in exile from 1975-1981, after the brutal assassination of her father Sheikh Mujibur Rahman and nearly every other member of her family. However, the situation is considerably different now. This time, Ms. Hasina came to India in 2024 fleeing mobs of protestors that overthrew her government, and has since been convicted by a tribunal for ordering a crackdown on thousands of students, and sentenced to death. In interviews, including to The Hindu , Ms. Hasina says she hopes to return to Bangladesh to argue her case and rebuild her party, the Awami League, but that is hardly likely, given the anger against her amongst the polity, and bipartisan consensus to ban the Awami League from politics. Despite the harsh rhetoric it employs against her, the BNP government is unlikely to wish for her return, as it would have to begin execution proceedings against the 79-year-old former Prime Minister, with international opposition to such a move expected to be voluble. Not doing so would only strengthen its opposition party, the Jamaat-e-Islami, that has accused the Rahman government of soft-pedalling the issue. The government must also worry about possible protests and violence within the country in the event Ms. Hasina returns.

The situation puts the Modi government in a spot. Ever since Ms. Hasina announced plans to return, during a virtual press conference held in Delhi on August 5 this year, Delhi-Dhaka ties have been on a downslide. The government’s decision not to prevent Ms. Hasina from addressing the press, where she used the opportunity to soundly criticise PM Rahman, meant the abrupt cancellation of the Bangladesh PM’s visit. Next month, the Indo-Bangladesh Ganga Water treaty is set to expire, and talks on its extension have also become a casualty. Ms. Hasina has been an honoured guest in India, and the government cannot physically restrain her from taking the flight to Dhaka or travelling to the land border at Petrapole to cross over. Nor can it wash its hands of her situation once she crosses over. New Delhi must redouble its diplomatic efforts on improving bilateral ties while also ensuring Ms. Hasina’s welfare.

articles.title: New deal: On COP31 and lofty climate goals
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: The 31st Conference of Parties (COP) began this week in Antalya, Türkiye. Hosted by Türkiye and negotiations presided over by Australia, the run-up to the gathering saw ministerial delegations visit Fiji and Tuvalu. This was to serve as a stark reminder of the purpose of COPs, namely that it was small island nations that are most vulnerable to warming from rising greenhouse gas emissions. However, the opening days have belied this sense of urgency. Prominent world leaders, even from the European countries who as a group champion the cause most vociferously, have chosen to skip the meet. The agenda and pre-summit expectations suggest that the main concerns this year are likely to be about delivering on existing commitments such as delivering $300 billion a year by 2035, which was decided at COP29 in Baku, as well as the COP30 call to triple the adaptation finance during that interval. However, deciding how these climate funds will practically flow has been deferred to COP32. The second global stocktake, a periodic check on progress under the Paris Agreement, begins at COP31, but the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) has dithered on a timeline for the next reports that will serve as the scientific push to policy makers to accelerate efforts towards keeping a rise in temperatures below 2°C, and more ambitiously 1.5°C.

The previous edition of COP30 concluded without a formal roadmap away from fossil fuels — a step back from the COP28 consensus in Dubai. There is a voluntary roadmap ahead of COP31 but it is out of the formal negotiating text. In the background of the West Asia war, the withdrawal of the United States from the Paris Agreement and financial strain writ large over Europe, funds are a challenge as evidenced in the recent Loss and Damage fund approval to Nepal of $21 million when the ask is in billions. COP31 president, Murat Kurum has laid an electrification target, which is to raise electricity’s share from 23% of total energy consumption to 35% by 2035. India has already refused to sign such a pledge and insisted on predictable climate finance, technology transfer, and nationally determined approaches to climate mitigation. These negotiations have a character of their own and deliberating nations must strive to get nations to deliver on past promises rather than commit to new lofty targets.

articles.title: Visions of the future: On this year’s Booker Prize
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: A defining feature of the world today is that knowledge is proliferating and societies are struggling to agree on what is happening. AI models have significantly catalysed this devolution, allowing bad actors to flood spaces ranging from the research literature to public airwaves with questionable information, and drawing the attention of governments worldwide to the security implications of such a potent technology. The Booker Prize for M. John Harrison’s The End of Everything , a novel about a sense-defying alien invasion and the unsettling prospect of un-understandability it confronts humans with, effectively acknowledges the centrality of the AI question both through the book’s substance and the judges’ choice. A consequence of rampant AI use has been an assault on people’s attention span as well as the ability to make sense of new claims, so much so that reliable, verifiable meaning has become a premium entity. The novel, on the other hand, attempts to diagnose a post-meaning world in which people are only left to look inward. The Prize is also a long-overdue victory for the merits of science fiction, a genre that Harrison helped shape from the late 1960s, and one that English literature’s top honours have repeatedly overlooked. That said, the novel itself is far from being its best example, including because Harrison’s diagnosis lets technology and the practice of power off the hook for their failures.

One of the judges said she had also sought a book “only a human being could write”, but defending a novel for its ability to thumb its nose at the machines is unfair to the literary enterprise and betrays a wider public anxiety about AI, especially over the lack of consensus about its proper place in society. OpenAI has been aggravating these deliberations among mathematicians by using its machines to make headway, in record time, on problems that have been unsolved for decades, without also contributing to mathematical education and research. Anthropic , the American company known for its Claude AI model, has announced its IPO with a surprising proposed valuation of $1.4 trillion . Since much of this is pegged on speculative future demand for AI services, the same absence of consensus leaves room for investors to imagine an enormous market for Anthropic’s products and invest to help the company realise them, thus narrowing the space for society to deliberate on all competing visions of the future. And while The End of Everything , with its philosophy of pragmatic absurdism, offers poor guidance on how to keep that space open, doing so ultimately remains one of the most important unfinished tasks before the world today.

articles.title: Milking power: On the overturning of Gokul Dairy cooperative mandate
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: Amid a nationwide outcry over electoral malpractices, with fresh evidence emerging every day, the BJP government in Maharashtra has gone a step further in overturning a popular mandate through an executive fiat. It approved changing the Maharashtra Cooperative Societies Act through an ordinance on November 4 — which the Governor promulgated on November 6 — with the immediate effect of facilitating the takeover of the Kolhapur District Cooperative Milk Producers’ Union, popularly known as Gokul Dairy , by the BJP and its allies. A Congress-led panel won 13 of the 25 elected seats on the board of the cooperative on October 19. Gokul, which is one of Maharashtra’s most influential cooperative institutions, has an annual turnover of around ₹4,000 crore and is linked to several lakh milk producers in western Maharashtra. The BJP had set its eyes on the cooperative sector as yet another arena of its political dominance, creating a Ministry of Cooperation under Home Minister Amit Shah. While that plan of controlling cooperatives continues to play out through various means, the overturning of an election clearly won by the Congress-led Opposition marks a new level of brazenness by the BJP, and of the impunity its actions continue to receive from the judiciary.

The Congress-backed Rajarshi Shahu Shetkari Samvichari Aghadi, led by Satej Patil, won 13 of the 25 elected seats on the Gokul board. On October 29, the election of the chairman was deadlocked after the BJP-allied members did not participate, and the meeting fell short of the required quorum of 14 members. The directors allied to the Congress and its partners subsequently declared Shashikant Patil Chuyekar as chairman, but the administration refused to recognise the election as quorum requirements had not been met. The amendment made through the ordinance allowed the government to nominate five directors to certain large cooperative institutions, with four nominees receiving voting rights. To be sure, four were nominated immediately to the Gokul board, and they voted with the BJP and its partners to elect a chairman on November 10 . The mandate of the cooperative’s members had been 13-12 in favour of the Congress and its allies, but it turned 16-13 in favour of the BJP and its partners, with the appointment of members with voting rights by the State government. Those defeated approached the Bombay High Court on November 9 to restrain the government-nominated directors from voting, but the High Court did not grant that relief. The diffidence of the judiciary in intervening in favour of democratic principles is turning out to be a matter of concern . The overturning of the popular mandate in Gokul Dairy cannot be seen as an isolated incident. It is yet another instance in a troubling pattern of state power silencing the people’s choice.

articles.title: Caste and class: On OBC reservation
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: If public resources are to dismantle both caste hierarchy and class inequality, OBC reservation should resist the notion that caste disadvantage makes economic differences among OBC families irrelevant. The ‘creamy layer’ rules are responsible for identifying those OBC members who have advanced sufficiently to no longer require affirmative action. However, the government has implemented them inconsistently. The Supreme Court in March corrected one inconsistency, that the government cannot hold the salary alone of an OBC candidate’s parent as evidence of social advancement. In Indra Sawhney (1992) , the Court upheld the government’s 27% reservation for OBC candidates in central government services if it also excluded economically advanced sections, i.e., the creamy layer, among OBCs. Following the equivalence requirement issued in 1993, the Department of Personnel & Training (DoPT) issued a “clarification” in 2004 that the government used, from around 2015, to deny dozens of OBC candidates who had cleared the Civil Services Examination their benefits because their parents’ salaries exceeded the official threshold due to pay revisions that did not always reflect changes in occupational status. The Cabinet also approved equivalence guidelines in 2017 but a parliamentary committee criticised it over a number of issues.

In Rohith Nathan (2026) , the Court rightly rejected the government’s use of the 2004 “clarification” to arbitrarily exclude OBC candidates based on their parents’ salaries alone. However, the government stalled service allocations following the 2025 examination and appealed that retrospectively applying the ruling would create administrative chaos. On November 6, the Court conceded that it had not asked the government to reopen completed selections, as it could set workers against one another while leaving government misapplication unaddressed. A proactive policy is essential now as the government must create supernumerary posts for legitimate claimants and apply the 1993 rules to pending allocations without vouchsafing these remedies for only those who can afford litigation. Access to public employment continues to be grossly unequal: per the 2024-25 DoPT Annual Report, OBC representation in central government employment was 26.3% but declined steadily towards higher positions. As the Justice G. Rohini Commission also indicated, the benefits of reservation are distributed unevenly among OBC communities. However, the report, submitted in 2023, is still not in the public domain. The coming Census includes caste enumeration but policymakers also need data on each caste’s education, occupations, assets, and landholdings. Defending redistribution among caste groups while ignoring major inequalities within them, and constraining OBC reservation assuming relatively more high-income families capture the benefits without first establishing the extent and the causes are equally difficult to justify.

articles.title: Police aspirant found dead, boyfriend and relatives arrested in Mahabubabad
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: A 24-year-old woman preparing to join the Telangana Police was found dead at her house in Nadivada village of Mahabubabad district on November 12. Police have arrested her boyfriend Anil and his relatives in connection with the case.
The deceased, Sushmita belonged to the Madiga community. Her parents, Kumaraswamy and Sukanya, found her dead after returning home with their other daughter from a function that evening.

According to Deputy Superintendent of Police N. Tirupathi Rao, Sushmita left behind an 18-page note accusing Anil, who belonged to the Goud community, of refusing to marry her despite being in a relationship with her for nearly two years. She had accused him of initially promising to marry her but later backing out, citing opposition from his family and friends over their different castes.

In the note, Sushmita blamed Anil for her death and expressed regret over not being able to fulfil her ambition of joining the police force and making her parents proud. Police registered a case under the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act and for abetment to suicide against 11 persons, including Anil, his parents and other relatives. Further investigation is underway.
(Roshini suicide prevention helpline number are: 8142020033/44 and 040 66202000/2001.)

fullParagraphs: The Vijayawada Press Club and the NTR Memorial Trust Blood Centre are jointly organising a free blood donation camp on November 16 to mark National Press Day.
The camp will be held at the Press Club in Gandhi Nagar from 10 a.m. to 1 p.m. on Monday. CR Media Academy Chairman Alapati Suresh Kumar will be the chief guest and inaugurate the camp.

Donors will be issued certificates by the NTR Trust. Those holding the certificates can avail themselves of blood transfusion services from the Trust at half the regular price if they need them in the future, according to a release.
Journalists willing to donate blood have been requested to register their names in advance at the Press Club.

articles.title: BJP accuses Congress of double standard on women’s issues
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) on Saturday (November 14, 2026) accused the Congress of following a double standard on the issue of women’s dignity, safety and empowerment by publicly advocating women’s rights while “remaining silent” on accusations of misconduct against its own leaders.

At a press conference, BJP MP Bansuri Swaraj referred to Jharkhand Congress MLA Bhushan Bara, who has been accused of sexually assaulting a 14-year-old tribal girl; MP Vimal Akoijam, who faces allegations of sexual harassment in Jawaharlal Nehru University (JNU); and Uttarakhand party leader Harak Singh Rawat, who was earlier accused of raping a woman from Assam.
The woman, who claimed that she became pregnant after the alleged abuse, has now demanded a DNA test on her son. The three Congress leaders have denied the accusations.

Ms. Swaraj questioned the “silence” of senior Congress leaders, saying that under the leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi, the BJP government was empowering women to become self-reliant and nation-builders, while the Congress was limited to raising slogans.

She alleged that the Congress continued to “repeatedly insult women”. “Tomorrow also marks the birth anniversary of Bhagwan Birsa Munda ji and Janjatiya Gaurav Diwas. On such an occasion, it is deeply shameful that Jharkhand Congress MLA Bhushan Bara is facing serious allegations of sexually assaulting a 14-year-old tribal girl,” she said.

“It is surprising that the Congress, which raises hollow slogans such as ‘Smash the Patriarchy’, along with its Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi, Priyanka Gandhi, Sonia Gandhi and Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge, has once again chosen to maintain silence on this matter,” she alleged.

“All these cases are distinct from one another, whether it is the rape of a tribal girl, the appointment of Vimal Akoijam as co-chairman of manifesto committee, or the appointment of Harak Singh Rawat as chairman of the election management committee in Uttarakhand. However, one thing is common to all these cases: the conspicuous silence of the Congress party and Rahul Gandhi,” she said.

articles.title: Opposition parties, civil rights groups come together to save voters’ rights in West Bengal
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: Calling for people whose names were unlawfully deleted from the electoral rolls during the special intensive revision (SIR) exercise to raise their voices, several opposition parties and civil rights groups on Saturday (November 14, 2026), announced a joint platform in West Bengal to save the rights of all voters.

The members of the ‘Sara Bangla Votadhikar Rokkha Jukto Moncho’ (All Bengal Joint Forum to Safeguard Voting Rights) also invited all opposition political parties to attend a mass convention in Kolkata on November 21.

“We are inviting all the opposition political parties to attend the convention. The voters whose names have been unlawfully deleted from the electoral rolls are also being called upon to raise their voices through this platform to protect their constitutional right,” said economist and Congress leader Prasenjit Bose.

Making an official announcement of the platform at a press conference on Saturday (November 14, 2026), its members said representatives of various parties, including the Congress, Mamata All India Trinamool Congress, Communist Party of India (CPI), Communist Party of India (Marxist) (CPIM), along with civil rights groups like Bharat Jodo, Nagarik Rakkha Mancha, and Association for Protection of Civil Rights (APCR), will be present at the November 21 convention. People whose names have been deleted in the Special Intensive Revision will also join, they said.

Mr. Bose said the united platform will raise six major questions to the Election Commission of India (ECI). “We want to know how long it will take the tribunals to dispose of lakhs of appeals pending before them. The State Election Commission must answer whether all the 22 lakh voters, who appealed to the tribunal for inclusion of their names, will be deprived of their voting rights in the upcoming municipality and panchayat elections,” he said.

The SIR process in West Bengal was held from October 2025 to February 2026, just before the Assembly election, which saw the Bharatiya Janata Party come to power in the State for the first time. The names of over 91 lakh electors were deleted from the electoral rolls, accounting for a drop of about 13% in the number of voters in the State from before the start of the exercise.

According to an affidavit filed in the Supreme Court by the ECI in September, of the 27 lakh electors excluded from the electoral rolls on the ground of ‘logical discrepancies’, 22 lakh have filed appeals before the tribunal challenging the decision. The ECI’s affidavit added that 16.10 lakh appeals have also been filed against inclusions during the SIR. This puts the total number of appeals pending before the SIR tribunals at 38 lakh.

The new platform alleged that the applications for inclusion of 16 lakh names were generated by former Chief Electoral Officer (CEO) Manoj Agrawal and demanded clarification on the appeals. It also sought information from the ECI on the number of eligible voters whose names have so far been restored in the electoral roll through Form 6 (used for inclusion of new voters) during the ongoing special summary revision (SSR).

“We have found that the former Chief Electoral Officer (CEO), Manoj Agrawal, generated these applications against 16 lakh names. We want to know who are these people, why these applications have been issued against their names despite being included in the voters’ lists in the SIR. Do they belong to any specific community or any particular region? How have their names been chosen?” asked retired Indian Administrative Service officer and former Rajya Sabha member Jawhar Sircar.

articles.title: Police question Abhishek Banerjee for three hours over post against CEC
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: The West Bengal Police questioned Mamata All India Trinamool Congress (MAITC) general secretary Abhishek Banerjee for over three hours on Saturday (November 14, 2026) in connection with a social media post against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.
Two days before the State Assembly election result was published, the Diamond Harbour MP had put up a post on his X handle calling the CEC a "puppet of the Gujarati gang".
A first information report was lodged at the Bhawanipore police station on May 27 against him for allegedly hurting the sentiments of the Gujarati community through the post.

On receipt of summons, he reached the Bhawanipore police station around 1.30 p.m. After leaving the police station, Mr. Banerjee said he was not afraid and stood by what he said. “Investigating agencies are doing their job. I have not run away. I respect the law enforcement agencies. But, I stand by what I said in the post. I had quoted a post by BJP leader Amit Malviya and called the BJP ‘anti-Bengal’,” he said.

Mr. Banerjee said Mr. Malviya had earlier said that there was no language called Bengali and that it was actually ‘Bangaldeshi’ language. “BJP is the party that destroyed the statues of Vidyasagar (social reformer-writer) stopped Central funds for West Bengal, and insulted the Bengali culture several times,” he said.
The development comes days after the Kolkata Municipal Corporation razed a tin shade and a boundary gate of Mr. Banerjee’s Kalighat residence.

Mr. Banerjee was also summoned by the Girish Park Police station on November 20 for making critical comments against the Paschim Medinipur SP. He had accused the SP of acting as per the “ruling party’s words”.

He has also appeared before the Crime Investigation Department (CID) twice in connection with a signature forgery case. On June 15, the Enforcement Directorate questioned him in Kolkata in connection with a money-laundering probe into the multi-crore West Bengal primary teachers’/school jobs recruitment scam.

articles.title: Keralam Speaker’s absence from endosulfan victims’ memorial event triggers row
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: Keralam Assembly Speaker Thiruvanchoor Radhakrishnan’s absence from the unveiling of a sculpture honouring endosulfan victims in Kasaragod has triggered a row, with the Speaker and the district panchayat offering conflicting accounts of the happenings.

The Speaker was scheduled to unveil the 40-foot-tall sculpture, titled ‘Victims,’ created by sculptor Kanayi Kunhiraman at the Kasaragod district panchayat office on Friday. However, he skipped the function and attended another programme in the neighbouring Kannur district. His absence drew criticism from artists and public representatives, including Manjeswaram MLA A.K.M. Ashraf.

Speaking to reporters on Saturday, Mr. Radhakrishnan said he had waited until the last minute for proper communication from the organisers before cancelling his ticket. “As there was no communication from the organisers, I cancelled the ticket. Later, I booked another ticket and went to Kannur,” he said. He said he had expected the organisers to explain the circumstances but decided to clarify his position himself as they remained silent. “It was a very unfortunate incident. I have nothing more to say,” he added.

However, Kasaragod district panchayat president Sabu Abraham disputed the Speaker’s account, maintaining that he had been informed about the event through proper channels and that the organisers had made every effort to secure his participation. Mr. Abraham said the invitation was initially extended through Uduma MLA K. Neelakandan, who had met the Speaker during the Assembly session and obtained a date for the programme. The district panchayat subsequently sent an official letter to the Speaker’s office. After the programme was finalised at a board meeting on November 6, the organisers sent the detailed schedule and a formal communication to the Speaker, he said.

Mr. Abraham said he had personally telephoned the Speaker on the night of November 11 and requested him to attend the event. He also contacted the Speaker’s private secretary the following morning to enquire about his travel arrangements. “The private secretary advised me to contact the Speaker directly, following which I called him and explained the arrangements. During the conversation, the Speaker mentioned certain confusion and also referred to the MLA not answering his phone,” he said.

He said he had assured the Speaker that all arrangements were in place and urged him to attend, pointing out that the occasion marked an important milestone in the career of Mr. Kunhiraman.Mr. Abraham said he had also contacted Mr. Neelakandan the following morning and asked him to speak to the Speaker to ensure his participation.
